A conjugate prior gives the posterior in closed form:
updating the prior only changes the family's parameters.
In @exm-normal-normal,
a Gaussian prior for a Gaussian mean gave a Gaussian posterior.
For a related video lecture, see Richard McElreath's
[*Garden of Forking Data*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pGVkCWlXnlg)
(Statistical Rethinking 2026, Lecture A02).
